## 1. What this is

Plain-text prompts for the {{scenario_count}} writing tasks that come up most often in research papers, one recommended prompt per task, all in [section 4](#4-prompts). Copy one into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi or any other chat model. Most are collected or adapted from public projects; every entry names its source and license.

> [!NOTE]
> The [full catalog](CATALOG_EN.md) has {{candidate_count}} candidate templates, including alternatives for most scenarios. Some candidates contain several short prompts; pick the one that fits. There is also a [web version](https://dengzhe-hou.github.io/research-writing-prompts/) with search, category filters and one-click copy.

## 2. Pick one in 30 seconds

{{quick_pick}}

**Three common paths**

1. Chinese draft → `1.1` Chinese → English → `2.1` English polish → `6.1` self-review.
2. Results table → `5.1` experiment analysis → `5.2` figure choice → `4.5` results and discussion.
3. Reviewer comments → `6.2` point-by-point response → `6.3` cover letter.

## 3. How to use

1. Find your task in section 4, open it and use the copy button on the code block, or search the [web version](https://dengzhe-hou.github.io/research-writing-prompts/).
2. Paste the prompt into a chat model and replace the bracketed placeholders (for example `[在此处粘贴你的中文草稿]`) with your text.
3. Replace `【你的领域，如计算机科学、心理学】` and `【目标期刊或会议】` with your field and target venue, for example “cognitive neuroscience” and “NeuroImage”.
4. To check every edit, add a line `MODE: diff` at the end of the input. The 2.x polishing and 3.x shorten/expand prompts then return a unified diff instead of a full rewrite.
5. Models can invent numbers and references. Verify every number, citation and page number. Placeholders such as `[待补]`, `[待检索]` and `[to verify]` are for you to fill; they are not verified content.

## 6. Before you use them

- `1.1` uses the present tense for methods and conclusions by default. Fields such as psychology report their own methods and results in the past tense; the prompt says to follow the field's convention, and you can adjust it further.
- The primary candidate for `4.x` is the structured version; the alternative is the original one-line quick version. When time is short, draft with the one-liner, then switch to the structured version for constraints.
- `5.5` now returns two parts: a layout spec (modules, arrows, labels) and an image-model prompt. When the figure contains a lot of text or must be exact, use a vector tool such as [figures4papers](https://github.com/ChenLiu-1996/figures4papers).
- `4.9`, `5.2`, `5.3` and `5.4` have a single candidate; no alternative is missing.
- The field and venue placeholders are not decoration. Replacing them changes the output noticeably.

## 7. Skills for multi-step work

For multi-step work such as literature reviews, drafting a whole paper or rebuttals in Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, install the skills from these projects:

- [nature-skills](https://github.com/Yuan1z0825/nature-skills): skills for Nature-style polishing, writing, figures, peer review, responses to reviewers and more
- [ARIS](https://github.com/wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep): a full set of skills from idea discovery and literature review to paper writing, review and rebuttal, aimed at machine-learning research
- [humanizer](https://github.com/blader/humanizer): removes signs of AI writing from English text
- [humanizer-zh-academic](https://github.com/redbaronyyyyy-eng/humanizer-zh-academic): removes AI-style phrasing from Chinese academic text
- [academic-research-skills](https://github.com/Imbad0202/academic-research-skills): research, writing, review, revision and finalization (CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial use only)
